title: Split CLI run function into per-command handlers in main.rs
summary: Refactor crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs so no function exceeds 200 lines (run is 549) and the file stays under its production-line limit, by moving each large Command arm of run into its own handler function (or a new sibling module). Behavior is unchanged. The audience is code health and the maintainers.

defaults_applied.how: cargo test and clippy must pass
One focused refactor of a single file
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy, fmt --check
The long function is split by command, not trimmed by cosmetic edits
Criteria run the test suite and --help rather than checking that functions exist
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs; run (line 1016 to about 1697) is one match over Command with inline arms (Ask, Retry, Propose, ScoreJev, Review, AcceptProposal, RejectProposal, ApproveWork, and more), each calling open(..), an Athena method, then print_json or display::*. Helpers sit above it (lines 572-1014). Sibling modules exist: drain.rs, display.rs, wiring.rs, hooks.rs, decisions.rs in crates/athena-cli/src/.

Approach: extract each long arm into a private fn taking the destructured fields and returning Result<u8>; keep run as a thin dispatcher. Group arms into a sibling module only if that is needed to get the file under the 1500-line landing-frequency limit. Do not change CLI output, exit codes, or clap definitions.
No records or data files are added, so the records allow-list is unaffected. No refusal rule is added or changed.
Governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, clippy config) are not touched.
The 1290 production lines are already under 1500 and 2000; the breach is the per-function limit, so run must drop to 200 lines or fewer, and so must every new function.

acceptance_criteria.text: In crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs (and any new module), no function exceeds 200 lines; run is a dispatcher of roughly 200 lines or fewer. Check by reading the file.

The diff is a pure restructuring: the Command enum, clap definitions, message strings and exit codes are unchanged, and the existing tests in main.rs and crates/athena-cli/tests are not modified or removed.
Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`. All existing tests pass, including tests/binary.rs and tests/proposals.rs, which exercise CLI output.
Run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.
Run `cargo run -p athena-cli -- --help`. The output matches the pre-change output, so the subcommand list is unchanged.

out_of_scope: Any behavior, CLI surface, or output change
Changes to other files over limits
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml or code-health limits
